news.hook: Old clips of Randy Moss at Marshall show him leaping over defenders and rumbling 90 yards for touchdowns, leaving fans in awe of plays that look downright unfair.
news.name: Randy Moss's Marshall Highlights Still Stun Fans Decades Later
news.summary: After off-field issues sidelined him from bigger programs, Moss transformed Marshall University into a powerhouse, catching 55 touchdowns in 28 games across two dominant seasons. As a freshman in 1996, he helped the Thundering Herd go undefeated for a Division I-AA national title; the next year in Division I-A, he won the Biletnikoff Award and finished fourth in Heisman voting. Iconic moments like his screen-pass score against Army and contested grabs popularized 'getting Mossed'—the art of a receiver towering over defenders—a term born in those college days and carried into his Hall of Fame NFL career.

news.summary: On his show, Wright argued Allen lacks a true signature victory, with many recalling defeats to QBs like Joe Burrow, Bo Nix, and Patrick Mahomes, despite acknowledging the 2021 Wild Card rout of the Patriots. Defenders countered by touting Allen's regular-season wins record over seven seasons, clutch comebacks, and praise from Mike Tomlin, who called him the top QB for critical moments. As the Bills face the Texans on September 13—where Allen is 1-4 historically—the debate underscores his elite stats against the push for deeper playoff runs.

Texans fans recalled close calls for J.J. Watt's MVP bids and C.J. Stroud's rookie honors, and Jaguars backers pointed to their Walter Payton Man of the Year as a bright spot.
